chapter: Brass bands and the ERA/WPA band
title: Night jobs and advertising on trucks
summary: Public appearances brought extra dance jobs, and the bands advertised on trucks.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Any fellows got any extra jobs on the side playing ever any time?
Well, people would come like that, they would see us in the air, go to the hospital and all like that, play for the sick and everything, Marine Hospital, all the big institutions. We would play.
I mean, at night though, sometimes you all, some of you able to play small dance jobs around?

Oh, at night if we wasn't playing, we was going to get out anyhow, because we had plenty. Yeah. At that time, everybody was out, so we had to get out, yeah. But we would be working. Yeah. Yeah, we would be working. Always would do something. Then it was much better, I'll tell you, because we would always keep going. But the people liked it and they know you played with the band and they see y'all, then you always would have, then you'd get more work because people would see y'all in the night.

Yeah. Always kept up with something. Yeah. And then we'd go to different institutions, the doctors, like the Marine Hospital, they see us in there and like us, well they come and ask, well which one of you boys have a band and y'all have a little group? We'd give them a card. They're a party. Yeah, and they give a party, well they hire us. At the charity, they do also the same thing, you see, like that. But likewise, we played back at the prison, well the captain back there, they get together, they give something. They'd hurry up, they'd give out, well they'd give a job. But it always was something for us to do because of advertising as you're getting out. Yeah.
Did you ever play on the wagons, well I think I was about advertising?
Well I played on the truck, I'll tell you. I played on the truck.
Yeah, a lot of trucks we'd advertise on trucks.
